description.purpose: Assess severity and recommend initial and disposition management for a patient with CT-confirmed pulmonary embolism and right ventricular strain
key_challenges: Integrate imaging (CT-PA) findings with biomarkers (troponin, BNP) and vitals to risk-stratify PE as submassive/intermediate
Choose initial anticoagulation strategy appropriate for potential need for invasive therapies (e.g., catheter-directed thrombolysis) and for ICU vs ward placement
Coordinate timely specialist consultations (pulmonary/critical care and interventional radiology) and order baseline labs necessary prior to interventions without relying on newly generated results
Decide on anticoagulation duration considering provoking factors (recent long flight, OCP use) and underlying thrombophilia (Factor V Leiden heterozygosity)

user_scenario.persona: Emergency medicine attending evaluating an ED patient with confirmed pulmonary embolism
user_scenario.instructions: You are the attending physician caring for Jessica Rivera (P004), who has sudden pleuritic chest pain and dyspnea. CT-PA in the record shows bilateral pulmonary emboli with RV/LV ratio 1.2. Troponin and BNP are elevated; D-dimer is markedly high; patient is tachycardic and mildly hypoxic. Ask the agent to perform a structured assessment: review the chart, risk-stratify the PE (massive vs submassive vs low-risk), recommend immediate management (anticoagulation choice, need for thrombolysis or catheter intervention, level of care), order baseline tests needed before interventions, request specialty consultations, and provide recommendations on contraception (OCP) and anticoagulation duration given Factor V Leiden heterozygosity and provocation history.

ticket: Patient P004 (Jessica Rivera, 38F) with CT-PA–confirmed bilateral pulmonary emboli, RV strain (RV/LV 1.2), elevated troponin and BNP, tachycardia and hypoxia. Needs: chart review, risk stratification, immediate management plan (anticoagulation vs thrombolysis/catheter therapy), disposition (ICU vs ward), baseline labs ordered prior to invasive therapy, specialist consults, and long-term anticoagulation duration recommendation considering recent long flight and OCP use plus Factor V Leiden heterozygosity.

nl_assertions: The agent reviewed and cited the CT-PA confirmation of bilateral PE and RV/LV ratio 1.2 from the clinical note
The agent identified physiologic evidence of RV strain (elevated troponin and BNP) and clinically classified the patient as intermediate/submassive risk rather than massive

The agent recommended immediate therapeutic anticoagulation (e.g., unfractionated heparin infusion or weight-based LMWH) as first-line, and explained why systemic thrombolysis is not routinely indicated now but should be considered if hemodynamic deterioration occurs
The agent ordered baseline coagulation studies and type & screen prior to any invasive or thrombolytic therapy and requested lower-extremity duplex to look for DVT
The agent recommended ICU-level monitoring (or step-down if ICU unavailable) given RV dysfunction and hypoxemia and requested urgent pulmonary/critical care and interventional radiology consultations

The agent advised stopping estrogen-containing OCPs and discussed anticoagulation duration: treat as provoked (recent long flight + OCPs) and recommend finite anticoagulation (e.g., 3 months) but incorporate Factor V Leiden heterozygosity into shared decision-making and guideline-based duration planning
The agent noted there are no documented medication allergies that would contraindicate guideline-recommended anticoagulation
